subject: general
question: Which state High Court in January 2025 has mandated that individuals in live-in relationships must sign a legal contract outlining financial responsibilities and childcare provisions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, the **Rajasthan High Court** directed that couples living in **live-in relationships** should sign a **legal contract** specifying their responsibilities.
 
• The suggested agreement should clearly mention **financial responsibilities**, **maintenance obligations**, and **childcare provisions**.
 
• The court observed that such contracts could help prevent **future disputes** between partners and provide legal clarity regarding rights and duties.
 
• The direction was made during hearings involving petitions filed by couples seeking **police protection** for their live-in relationship.
 
• The observation aimed to safeguard the interests of partners, particularly regarding **financial security** and **responsibility towards children**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct option is 3.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legal Status of Live-in Relationships in India**

 
 
• Live-in relationships are not illegal and have been recognised by the **Supreme Court of India** in several judgments.
 
• They are considered part of the **right to life and personal liberty under Article 21** of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Protection under Law**
 
 
• Women in live-in relationships are protected under the **Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005**.
 
• Children born from such relationships are considered **legitimate** under Indian law.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of the Court’s Observation**
 
 
• To establish **legal clarity** in live-in relationships.
 
• To ensure proper arrangements for **financial obligations** and **child welfare**.
